title: inbox popover always opens on the Notifications tab — with 0 notifications and 3 pending approvals the bell shows "3" and the panel says "You're all caught up"
body:
Filing gate: ① user-visible UX defect — `reach:` the header bell, measured; separate card under the maintainer's quota exception (provenance below).
Reader: objectui triage first-touch → `domain:ui` lane (`packages/app-shell`); one PR.
Dedup (semantic search, open + closed, objectui): "inbox popover opens on empty notifications tab while badge counts pending approvals" → 1 hit, closed duplicate (objectui#4156, an empty dropdown with unread rows — a different defect).

Environment: framework `ce577ec4` showcase booted with `objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin` on its own port and SQLite file; console = objectui `f9f4a62d` (`apps/console` Vite dev server, and a production `vite build` for timings); Chromium 141 headless, 1440×900, seeded admin.

## Repro

1. Stock showcase boot: the seeded admin has 0 notifications and 3 pending approvals.
2. The header bell shows the badge "3". Click it.
3. Actual: the popover header reads "3 total · 0 notifications + 3 pending approvals", the active tab is "Notifications" and its body is "You're all caught up"; the three items are behind the "Approvals 3" tab.

## Where

`packages/app-shell/src/layout/InboxPopover.tsx` — `const [tab, setTab] = useState<'notifications' | 'approvals' | 'activity'>('notifications')`: the initial tab is fixed, independent of where the badge's count comes from.

## Expected

The popover opens on the tab that holds what the badge counted (Approvals here), or the first non-empty tab; "You're all caught up" is never the first thing shown under a non-zero badge.

Provenance: filed as a separate card on the maintainer's explicit instruction in the dispatching session, which lifts the per-fire filing quota for this batch of seven, verbatim — 「重新思考以上和用户体验相关的问题，哪些需要立卡」 then 「分开立 7 张」. Found during a browser dogfood sweep of the console; companion checklist card objectstack-ai/objectui#11672. Filed by session `session_01WEARdKfDHDT7rTuEhLyT1k`.
